root_motivation: A chain's only ceiling was COMPOSE_CHILDREN_MAX (50 child calls) and a run's only stop was its deadline_s -- both cliffs with no warning and no per-tenant/per-call setting, so a looping chain looked healthy until the 50th call and a tenant had no way to ask for a cheaper run. ai-stack's mcp-query-budget-governor (~/projects/ai-stack @ 4ef6c22) already has the right shape for this: a small ledger over four Option dimensions, an alert at a configurable fraction, a hard stop at the limit. This build ports that ledger verbatim, threads it through compose_call (checked before each child, recorded after) and the run executor (built from the plan's defaults or a validated per-call override, persisted into progress_json.budget on every tick), and surfaces it in host.runs.get/list.
user_persona: A tenant running chains and async tool calls who wants a bound on what a run may spend (PRD user stories 1/2/4: a 10-child ceiling that halts the 11th step with a named error, a live fraction/verdict while still running, a synthetic panel task proving a recipe is cheap under a tiny budget); the operator watching the fleet, who wants free/pro defaults readable in plans.rs and runs listable by which ones crossed their budget (user story 3).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the ported ledger, When the seven carried-over unit tests run, Then they pass, including Alert at 0.8 and Exceeded at 1.0 on each dimension.

Given a chain of 12 steps and budget: {max_child_calls: 10}, When it runs, Then exactly 10 children execute, the run ends error with error_class budget_exceeded and error_data_json.dimension child_calls.
Given a free-plan tenant passing max_child_calls: 100, When host.tool_call is invoked, Then a validation error names the plan ceiling 20 and no run starts.
Given a chain whose third child returns a 400 KB result, When max_est_tokens is 150,000, Then the run halts before the fourth child with dimension est_tokens and used >= 100,000.
Given a running chain at 9 of 10 child calls, When host.runs.get is polled, Then progress_json.budget.fraction is 0.9 and verdict is alert.
Given a plain async host.tool_call with no budget, When it runs, Then budget.limits equal the plan defaults and verdict is ok on completion.
Given 200 child calls across runs, When timed, Then the budget check adds at most 1 ms p95 per child on the builder.
Given a run crossing 0.8, When it continues, Then one run.budget_alert event exists for it and alerted_at_unix is set once.
Given host.runs.list(verdict: "exceeded"), When called, Then only runs with budget_exceeded return.

Given prod after land, When a fresh tenant runs the docs-qa recipe's chain with budget: {max_child_calls: 3}, Then the run ends with budget_exceeded, and the same chain with plan defaults completes (Live; evidence: mcphost-1 healthz version after deploy plus both host.runs.get responses in the receipt under docs/receipts/).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned; needs a real deploy to production mcphost-1 and a post-deploy receipt, neither reachable from this build sandbox. Not in this dispatch's assigned AC list.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the five recipe proof scripts, When run under plan defaults on the builder, Then none ends with budget_exceeded.

scope: src/budget.rs (new): BudgetLimits/Dimension/Verdict/BudgetLedger (pure, ported), BudgetTracker (stateful: check/record/persist, the run.budget_alert alert, alerted_at_unix), resolve_and_validate, estimate_tokens.

src/plans.rs: Plan gains budget_max_child_calls/max_est_tokens/max_tool_latency_ms/max_wall_ms (free 20/200k/30k/60k, pro 50/2M/120k/600k) round-tripped through plans.toml, and Plan::budget_defaults().
src/kinds/mod.rs: CallCtx gains budget: Option<Arc<BudgetTracker>>; compose_call checks before each child dispatch (Exceeded refuses without dispatching) and records+persists after a successful one.

src/runs.rs: enqueue/enqueue_shared resolve+validate+store the run's effective limits in counters_json.budget.limits before insert; execute_job reconstructs the tracker, does an initial ok-verdict persist before dispatch, and threads it into the job's CallCtx; JobOutcome::Error now carries structured error_data through to finalize_run; list() gains a verdict filter.
src/handler.rs: host.tool_call validates a budget argument against the plan ceiling ahead of both sync and async dispatch; host.tool_call/host.runs.list wire schemas document budget/verdict.
src/errors.rs: budget_ceiling_exceeded (INVALID_PARAMS) and budget_exceeded (INVALID_REQUEST) jsonrpc_code mappings.
contracts/host-tools.v1.json: regenerated (mcphost contract dump) for both new wire arguments.
non_goals: Billing changes -- estimated tokens are for the budget only, never for metering (PRD's own non-goal 1); no calls.rs/billing.rs touched.
Model-token accounting inside a python or wasm tool -- the estimate stays chars/4 over the args/result the host itself sees (non-goal 2).
Raising plan ceilings -- resolve_and_validate can only lower a plan's own default, never exceed it (non-goal 3); AC3 is the direct proof.

Alert delivery to external channels -- progress_json is the surface; run.budget_alert rides the existing alerts.rs store (delivery to a configured webhook/inbox is that module's own pre-existing, unmodified behavior), not a new channel (non-goal 4).

additional.test_file_names_use_the_prd_test_prefix: test_prefix budget (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/budget_ac<NN>_<short_desc>.rs, one file per non-deferred AC.
additional.never_amend_a_committed_ac: Work AC-by-AC, one commit per AC (or per requirement with no AC of its own); a commit is never rewritten once the build has moved past it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does budget enforcement only wire into the async job path (runs::execute_job), never the synchronous call_published_tool path?
five_whys_trace.a: Every listed AC that exercises actual halting/recording (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC8, AC9) frames its scenario as 'the run' finalizing or being polled via host.runs.get while running -- only an async job has a 'running' row a concurrent poll can observe (a synchronous call's own runs row, per runs_ac05, is written only AFTER the call already finished). AC3's validation is the one budget-adjacent behavior that DOES apply to sync calls, and it's checked at host_tool_call's top regardless of the async flag, before either dispatch path runs.

five_whys_trace.q: Why store the resolved BudgetLimits in counters_json.budget.limits at enqueue time rather than re-resolving from the tenant's plan when execute_job later leases the row?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 3 says this in so many words ('the effective limits are stored on the run row in counters_json.budget.limits'), and it also closes a real race: a plan edit between enqueue and lease (the executor can sit behind other queued work) must not change a run's own budget out from under it after the caller already saw it accepted.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does compose_call's own child_calls counter never count the run's own top-level (non-composed) call?
five_whys_trace.a: COMPOSE_CHILDREN_MAX's existing atomic counter (ctx.compose_children) already only counts actual composed dispatches, never the root call -- mirroring that meant a plain non-chain async call (AC6) legitimately reports child_calls: 0 at completion, and an initial ok-verdict snapshot persisted before dispatch (independent of whether anything ever calls compose_call) is what makes AC6's budget.limits/verdict observable at all for a tool with no children.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AC11's uptime-probes leg drive tests/support/uptime_probes.rs's helpers directly instead of shelling out to examples/uptime-probes/proof.sh like the other four legs?
five_whys_trace.a: That recipe's probe tool declares network: "public", pro-plan-gated since PRD-mcphost-sandbox-egress-allowlist; proof.sh signs up its own fresh (free-plan) tenant via the public API and has no way to self-upgrade before its own publish step. Racing a Rust-side admin.plan_set against a bash subprocess's signup timing was considered and rejected as genuinely flaky; every existing in-repo runner for this recipe's real workload already solves this the same way this build does.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the run.budget_alert event key on run.budget_alert:<run_id> rather than a single shared run.budget_alert key?
five_whys_trace.a: alerts::raise collapses a repeated raise under the same key within its cooldown window (900s default) into one row's repeat_count -- a shared key across many different runs' alerts in the same test/window would make 'one event exists for THIS run' ambiguous to assert. Keying per run_id makes AC8's 'one run.budget_alert event exists for it' checkable in isolation regardless of what else alerted recently.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 6/AC8 says the alert event is 'written to the tenant's event stream the existing alert module owns' -- is that the per-tenant host.msg inbox, or alerts.rs's own (host-wide, key-scoped) alerts table?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: alerts.rs's own alerts table: it's the only store 'the existing alert module' (the phrase's own antecedent) owns, and admin.alerts.list is directly queryable/assertable. 'the tenant's event stream' is read as describing whose run the event is ABOUT (body.tenant_id/run_id), not a claim that a second, per-tenant-scoped store exists -- alerts.rs has none.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a per-call budget override apply to a synchronous (non-async) host.tool_call, or only to async/job dispatch?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Validation (AC3, budget_ceiling_exceeded) applies to both -- checked once at host_tool_call's top before either dispatch branch. Actual ledger enforcement (checking/recording per child) only wires into the async executor path (see five_whys #1); a synchronous chain call's own runs row is unaffected by this PRD.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD technical considerations: 'the budget's wall limit defaults to the deadline so they agree' -- does a per-call budget override get allowed to raise max_wall_ms past the plan's own deadline_s-derived ceiling?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No: max_wall_ms is validated against the plan's own budget_max_wall_ms default exactly like every other dimension (non-goal 3, 'lower only') -- this build does not additionally cross-check it against job_max_s/deadline_s, since the two are already the same numeric default per plan (60s/600s) and the PRD names no distinct ceiling for one over the other.
